strategyDefinition.books: independent long-below-anchor and short-above-anchor aggregation ladders
strategyDefinition.exit: each filled layer exits at the nearer of its fixed TP or the previous ladder level
strategyDefinition.reanchor: each book reanchors independently only after that book is flat or its cooldown ends
strategyDefinition.riskBudget: one shared marked-to-market account; half of the total gross budget reserved per side
strategyDefinition.intrabar: maintenance/stop first; existing TP before entries; no same-bar entry/TP
strategyDefinition.forecast: no directional or trend forecast is used

literature.citation: Willenbrock (2011), Diversification Return, Portfolio Rebalancing, and the Commodity Return Puzzle
literature.relevance: rebalancing is the source of diversification return; buy-and-hold is not equivalent

literature.citation: Witte (2015), Volatility Harvesting: Extracting Return from Randomness
literature.relevance: discrete random return models can turn excess volatility into growth while retaining implicit risks

literature.citation: Avellaneda and Stoikov (2008), High-frequency trading in a limit order book
literature.relevance: liquidity-provision quotes must account for inventory and price risk

literature.citation: Guéant, Lehalle and Fernandez-Tapia (2013), Dealing with the inventory risk
literature.relevance: market-making optimization is explicitly solved under inventory constraints

literature.citation: Chen, Chen and Jang (2025), Dynamic Grid Trading Strategy
literature.relevance: preprint derives near-zero expectation for a traditional static grid under simple assumptions and tests dynamic resetting

decision.rule: Positive validation, test, stressed-test and full medians with zero liquidations.
